rationale: The buyer is a pre-seed or seed-stage founder who has already paid for Stripe Atlas and has live users — a specific, reachable person with demonstrated spending behavior. The pain is severe (six-figure funds frozen at a critical moment) even if it is a low-frequency event. The product — a plain-language guide + payment-rails advisory — is buildable as a Claude-authored document or short advisory workflow, but the willingness to pay for a one-time guide vs. finding the answer free on HN is uncertain, keeping this in validate territory. Build gate for willingness_to_pay is borderline (6, meets the floor of 5); operational_autonomy meets the 7 floor. Validate first by landing page + waitlist to confirm people will actually pay.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a 'Stripe-safe Fundraising Rails' advisory pack: a structured guide + intake form that tells a founder exactly how to receive a pre-seed wire safely (Mercury direct, ACH from investor's bank, what NOT to run through Stripe), with a Claude-generated custom checklist based on their specific situation. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt + a Carrd/Typeform intake page + a Stripe payment link for a one-time $49-99 fee. Outreach goes to founders who post on Hacker News, Indie Hackers, or Reddit about Stripe account issues — the factory drafts those replies and queues them for Youval to approve before posting. Delivery is fully automated: intake form triggers Claude to generate and email the custom advisory pack. Support is handled by Claude replying to follow-up emails; Youval only approves the outreach batch and monitors edge cases. The one genuine risk: this is a frequently asked question that may have free community answers, so the paid validation test (even 10 sales) is essential before building further.
notes: All build gates technically pass (operational_autonomy=7, buildability_with_ai=8, buyer_clarity=7, willingness_to_pay=6). Total of 6.3 clears min_total_to_build (6.5 needed) narrowly — falls just short, so validate is correct. Defensibility is weak (3); a free blog post or HN comment can approximate the output. Validate demand with a real payment before investing further.
